DY2V: Sunn = emptiness, the thought-free state, the state in which no thought of attachment to Maya arises in the mind. Sandhia = (Skt. sandhya = the morning, noon and evening prayers of a Brahmin) the worship at morning, noon and evening that every Brahmin should perform. Devakar = O mine of light! (dev + akar). Adhpat = O Master! Aad = O root of the whole world! Samai = O all-pervading!

O Dev! O mine of light! O Master of the world! O root of all! O all-pervading Prabhu! (You are beyond Maya, so) keeping the mind clear of the thoughts of Maya (and staying joined to Your feet) — this is doing Your aarti.
Hear my prayer, Lord; You are the Divine Light of the Divine, the Primal, All-pervading Master.
O God, the Primal and all-pervading Master, you are the mine of light. Hear You, My present adoration.
O (dev) radiant God of gods, the (sunn) thought-free Vahiguru! I perform Your (sandhia) aarti. O Lord of all! I have known that the primal ground of all — Your being alone — pervades all of us.
36JV: Sidh = perfected yogis, yogis skilled in yogic practice. ||1||
Yogis skilled in yogic practice, even sitting in samadhi, have not found Your end; in the end they take Your refuge. ||1||
The Siddhas in Samaadhi have not found Your limits. They hold tight to the Protection of Your Sanctuary. ||1||
The adepts, in their trance have found not Your limit. They continue to cling o Your asylum.
Even the sidhs who stay in samadhi have not found Your end; so they too have come to cling to Your refuge. ||1||
50FZ: Ho bhai = O brother! Purakh niranjan aarti = the aarti of the all-pervading Prabhu who is free of Maya.
Walk on the path the Guru has shown, and perform the aarti of that Prabhu who is free of Maya and who pervades all,
Worship and adoration of the Pure, Primal Lord comes by worshipping the True Guru, O Siblings of Destiny.
O brother, worshiping the True Guru one is blessed with the present adoration of the Immaculate Lord.
O Niranjan Purakh ji! Accept the aarti I have performed, because I worship as a (bhai) lover of the Satguru.
GRD8: Thadha = standing. Nigam = the Vedas. Alakh = (Skt. alakshya = having no particular marks) the One who has no particular marks or features. ||1||Rahau||
the One who has no particular marks or features, whose virtues cannot be described, and at whose door Brahma stands reflecting on the Vedas. ||1||Rahau||
Standing at His Door, Brahma studies the Vedas, but he cannot see the Unseen Lord. ||1||Pause||
Standing at His door, Brahma reads the Vedas, but he can see not the Unseeable Lord. Pause.
What are You like? Brahma stands before You reflecting on the Vedas; O Unseen One! Even by him You cannot be seen. ||1||Rahau||
JJWY: Tat = wisdom. Bati = wick. Deh ujhara = light (of Your Name) in the body.
(The one who has understood this secret of aarti) has made wisdom the oil, the Name the wick, and the light (of the Name) within the body the lamp.
With the oil of knowledge about the essence of reality, and the wick of the Naam, the Name of the Lord, this lamp illluminates my body.
With the oil of truthfulness and the wick of the Lord's Name, I have made the lamp to illumine my body.
(Tat) The love described in the Shastras is the oil — or I have made the oil of discerning the real from the unreal — and I have made the Name the wick of repetition, and the body the clay lamp.
5YS1: Jagdis jot = the flame of the Name of the Lord of the world. Boojhanhara = the wise one. ||2||
He has lit this lamp (joined to) the light of the Prabhu, Master of the world. Only a rare wise one understands (the secret of the Prabhu's aarti). ||2||
I have applied the Light of the Lord of the Universe, and lit this lamp. God the Knower knows. ||2||
Applying the Light of the Lord of the World, I have lit the lamp. The Omniscient Lord alone knows this mystery.
O Lord of the world! When I lit it with Your flame, then (ujhara) light came; so by this lamp, O Vahiguru who understands all, we have (boojhai) come to know You. ||2||
MTGV: Panche sabad = all five sounds; the sound of five kinds of instrument (the five kinds are: stringed instruments, those covered with skin, those made of metal, the pot and the like, and those played by blowing. When all these kinds of instruments are played together, a most beautiful music arises that enraptures the mind). Anahad = unstruck, unbroken. Sange = right with, right within (one sees). Sarangpani = (sarang = bow; pani = hand) the One with a bow in His hand, who is also the destroyer of the whole world.
(O Prabhu! By the blessing of this aarti) I see You right with me (and within me a bliss is building as if) all five kinds of instruments are playing, unbroken (within me).
The Unstruck Melody of the Panch Shabad, the Five Primal Sounds, vibrates and resounds. I dwell with the Lord of the World.
The celestial strain of the five musical instruments resounds within me and I abide ever with the Lord of the world.

To know the One who lights up the five senses — the word and the rest — this is the (anahad) unbroken (sabad) music playing. Or: the instruments are the five kinds of unstruck sound; so in this way, O Sarangpani, we have found You with us.
716E: O Formless One, free of desire! O Sarangpani! I, Your servant Kabir, have also performed (just such an) aarti to You. ||3||5||
Kabeer, Your slave, performs this Aartee, this lamp-lit worship service for You, O Formless Lord of Nirvaanaa. ||3||5||
O Formless and Detached Lord, Your slave Kabir, performs such a worship of Yours.

Sri Kabir ji says: O Formless One, whose form is nirvana! I, the servant, have performed Your aarti in this way. ||3||5|| ☬ Setting out the cause of the mind's bondage and liberation, he utters his own experience:
